task.description:
You are on branch feature/WF03-ISS0881-20260929 (already checked out by the prior step; run `git branch --show-current` to confirm, and `git checkout feature/WF03-ISS0881-20260929` if not). Perform WF-03 Steps 0.5 (registry lookup) and 1 (diagnose) for docs/issues/ISS-0881.yaml in a single handoff, per docs/agents/workflows/WF-03_issue_resolving.md.

Step 0.5: read docs/issues/ISS-0873.yaml, ISS-0878.yaml, ISS-0879.yaml (all cited as precedent in ISS-0881.yaml's fix_direction field) in full. State in your result.summary whether ISS-0881's failure is the SAME root-cause mechanism as any of them (all three share a family resemblance -- platform-wide/unscoped reads racing a concurrent writer under scripts/test_parallel.sh contention -- but each has a distinct specific mechanism: ISS-0873 was a two-call bit-identical assertion racing a concurrent RetentionPolicy/Registration write; ISS-0879 was a throwaway test-support fixture row's visibility window leaking into an unscoped read; ISS-0878 was a process-local-only unique_integer collision across separate OS processes). Do not assume identity with any of them -- confirm or refute via your own investigation below.

Step 1: REPRODUCE the failure directly -- do not diagnose from ISS-0881.yaml's prose alone. Suggested approaches, in order of preference: (a) run the single failing test file repeatedly under real contention via `scripts/test_parallel.sh` (check its usage/flags first) or by running `mix test test/letflow/sandbox_pool_test.exs` concurrently alongside a separate full-suite background load (e.g. a second `mix test` process against the same Postgres instance) to recreate cross-partition contention against a single target test; (b) if true live reproduction proves impractical within reasonable time, high-confidence code-level analysis is acceptable PROVIDED you show your reasoning against the actual code paths involved (this is ISS-0873's own precedent, cited in ISS-0881.yaml's fix_direction, which reached resolution without live reproduction in that session -- but note ISS-0879's OWN resolution DID achieve isolated reproduction, so prefer that bar if you can reach it).

One lead worth checking, found during ORCH's own pre-dispatch read of the test file (verify or refute it yourself -- do not take it on faith, per HANDOFF_PROTOCOL.md's 'a handoff's factual premises are checkable, and may be wrong' -- this is ORCH's own claim in this dispatch, so it is exactly such a premise): `sandbox_schema_names/0` (test/letflow/sandbox_pool_test.exs:571-582) queries `information_schema.schemata` for ALL schemas platform-wide matching `sandbox\_%`, unscoped to this test's own run -- the same class of unscoped global read ISS-0873/ISS-0879 diagnosed elsewhere. The failing assertion `refute MapSet.member?(final, o_schema)` (line 1126) checks a SPECIFIC schema name (`o_schema`, minted via `Ecto.UUID.generate()`-derived construction, lib/letflow/sandbox_pool.ex:930-933 -- effectively collision-proof across partitions), not the whole set, so a same-name collision from another partition is implausible; investigate instead whether `wait_until_schema_dropped(o_schema)` (called at line 1121, immediately before the failing assertion) can report success while a SUBSEQUENT `sandbox_schema_names()` call still observes the schema -- e.g. a connection-level snapshot/isolation effect (a connection checked out via `query_without_holding`/`retry_query_once` holding a transaction snapshot opened before the DROP SCHEMA committed), a retry-masking effect in `retry_query_once/1` hiding an actual failed drop, or a genuinely different mechanism you find in the actual code. Read `wait_until_schema_dropped/1`, `query_without_holding/1`, and `retry_query_once/1`'s definitions in full before concluding.

Do NOT implement a fix. Write the diagnosis into result.summary: root cause (not just symptom), the exact mechanism, affected files, and what a fix needs to change. Complete the handoff with next_action: 'Route to CODE-DESIGNER for fix design' (or, if your investigation finds no real defect / cannot be reproduced or root-caused with reasonable confidence after genuine effort, state that plainly and recommend the no_defect path instead -- do not force a fix design on a diagnosis you don't actually have).
acceptance_criteria: Step 0.5: ISS-0873/0878/0879 read in full and each's relationship (or lack thereof) to ISS-0881's mechanism stated explicitly, with reasoning
Step 1: a real reproduction attempt was made and its actual outcome (succeeded / did not reproduce after N attempts) is reported with real command output, not assumed

A specific root-cause mechanism is named (function, race window, why the existing test's own defenses don't catch it) OR the investigation reaches a reasoned no-defect/inconclusive verdict with evidence, not a guess
No fix code written in this step
Handoff completed with a clear next_action for ORCH
